title: Biography revision dates now use the latest recorded content update
before: Article metadata and sitemap entries preferred the contribution section's date whenever that section existed, even if the biography had been revised more recently.
after: Article metadata and sitemap entries use the latest recorded biography, contribution, or evidence-note revision. A newer biography revision is no longer hidden by an older section date.
method: Code and data comparison; AI-assisted maintenance, not qualified human historical review.

title: Distinguished a saint's commemoration date from liturgical rank
before: Every biography's recurring date was labeled Feast Day, including optional memorials and traditional commemorations.
after: The date is labeled Commemoration. Calendar notes and an explanatory guide distinguish the directory's recurring date from a feast, memorial, or local observance in an approved liturgical calendar.
method: AI-assisted comparison with bishops' conference calendar guidance.

title: Explained Mary Magdalene's distinct identity and the 2016 feast-rank change
before: The biography already distinguished the Gospel figures, but had no separate evidence note explaining the older liturgical conflation or the meaning of feast rank.
after: Added source-linked evidence and calendar notes: the reformed liturgy concerns Mary of Magdala, and the 2016 change elevated the celebration's rank without moving July 22.
method: AI-assisted reading of the Holy See's 2016 explanation and preface commentary; no qualified human review credited.

title: Added a contemporary Catholic source identifying Christopher's river story as legend
before: The biography already identified the river crossing as legend and cited a historical reference work.
after: Added a directly linked Vatican News explanation and clarified that a July 25 saint-directory listing does not establish a universal obligatory memorial.
method: AI-assisted comparison with Vatican News and calendar guidance; no qualified human review credited.

title: Separated George's dragon legend, later patronage, and recurring calendar date
before: These distinctions were already present in the narrative but were not gathered in a dedicated evidence note.
after: Added source-linked guidance for reading the legend and medieval reception separately from evidence about the ancient martyr, with a note on local calendars.
method: AI-assisted source comparison; no qualified human review credited.

title: Explained John Paul II's optional memorial and anniversary choice
before: The short calendar note named October 22 and the inauguration of his pontificate.
after: Added a USCCB reference explaining the optional memorial's rank, its inclusion in the General Roman Calendar, and its distinction from his April 2 death anniversary.
method: AI-assisted comparison with the USCCB liturgical page; no qualified human review credited.
